summary: BBN's traffic statistics for the ARPANET hosts for January 1973, given as tables of packets output per host, split into traffic between sites and within a site, with daily averages. It is a usage record, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC shares a table of packets output by ARPANET hosts in January 1973. It separates traffic to other nodes from traffic within a node.

questions: what were the arpanet traffic statistics for january 1973
how are packets reported by host
subtitle: BBN's host-by-host packet counts for ARPANET traffic in January 1973.

tldr.problem: The Network community needed regular figures on traffic output by ARPANET hosts.
tldr.mechanism: The Host Throughput Summary lists packets output by host, separated into internode and intranode traffic, with totals and daily figures.
tldr.outcome: The report records January 1973 traffic, including some sites with fewer days of data or no traffic. It is a statistics memo, not a protocol.

sections.title: The January Report
sections.content:
A. McKenzie of BBN attaches the Host traffic statistics for January 1973. The attachment is titled Host Throughput Summary and reports packets output.

Hosts are grouped by site, with separate entries where a site has more than one host.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC presents a monthly packet-count report. Each row identifies a host whose traffic was counted.

sections.title: How to Read the Table
sections.content:
The table separates packets sent between nodes from packets sent within a node. It also gives a total for hosts and sites, an average daily internode count, and the number of days represented.

Most rows cover the full month, while some sites have fewer reported days; the report also marks hosts with no traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: The two traffic columns show whether packets crossed to another node or stayed within one. The days column shows how much data was available for a row.

sections.title: Totals and Averages
sections.content:
The table ends with totals for internode and intranode packets, daily averages, and averages per node-day. It also reports a packets-to-messages ratio for internode traffic.

The figures describe observed output during the reporting period and do not specify how hosts should communicate.
sections.plainLanguage: The report adds up the host figures and gives averages. These numbers are a snapshot of network traffic, not protocol rules.
